Ava (Design): Hey all — quick design review request for the Playground chat pane. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/playground-chat-ui (updated frames). Main items: streaming rendering, Stop vs Regenerate affordances, token counter placement, prompt library access. Looking for quick takes and any a11y nits. :eyes: Marcus (Frontend): Overall looks good. One worry: Stop and Regenerate sitting next to each other feels risky — accidental regen after a long output would be bad. Maybe primary action should change based on streaming state. Rina (PM): Agreed. Proposal: while streaming, primary = Stop; when complete, primary switches to Regenerate. Keeps send/regen separate flows. Also want keyboard shortcuts: Esc to stop, Ctrl/Cmd+R or button to regenerate. Jorge (Eng): Backend note: we support abort signals on stream. Client needs to send an AbortController signal and cancel any open SSE/WebSocket subscriptions before starting a new request. Example snippet:```js const ac = new AbortController(); fetch('/v1/generate', {signal: ac.signal}); // ac.abort() to cancel ``` Marcus (Frontend): Nice. UI idea: token counter as a compact pill in the top-right of the pane, expands on hover for breakdown (input / output / estimated cost). Keyboard: bind Esc for stop, Shift+Enter for send? Open to suggestions. Sam (Accessibility): A11y: streaming text should live in an aria-live region (polite) so screen readers announce updates without interrupting. When stream completes expose a clear status text (e.g., "Output complete") with role=status. Also ensure buttons have aria-labels. Example:```html
...streaming chunks...
``` Ava (Design): Copy language: prefer "Stop" over "Cancel/Halt" for clarity. For regenerate, tooltip full text "Regenerate response" but short button label "Regenerate". Token pill label should read "Estimated tokens: 123" in tooltip. Marcus (Frontend): Token precision question — we only approximate tokens client-side. Tooltip should say "Estimated tokens (approx): 120". Also add an icon for token meter so color alone isn't the only signal. Rina (PM): Prompt library placement: two options we considered — left rail persistent vs an inline drawer. Preference for inline drawer so you can browse and drag prompts into composer without losing context. Must support keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter to insert). Jorge (Eng): From perf side, dragging should not stream new API calls; treat prompt insertion as local text replace and debounce updates. Also ask that prompt objects include an id and a short preview to avoid heavy payloads in the UI. Sam (Accessibility): Focus trap requirement for drawer — when it opens focus goes to first item and user can tab through. Provide skip link to close drawer. Color contrast: token pill colors must meet 4.5:1 for normal text; add patterns or icons for color-blind users. Ava (Design): Accessibility nit also: ensure the Stop button has visible focus ring and is reachable via keyboard in 1 tab from composer. I'll update Figma to show focus states. lighthouse-bot: Automated accessibility scan: warning — low contrast on token meter (needs update). Marcus (Frontend): I'll prototype two variants tonight: (A) inline token pill to the right of composer controls, (B) floating token widget top-right. Will attach screenshots. Also will wire up AbortController example from Jorge. Rina (PM): Decision for next sprint: inline token pill (right of controls) + tooltip with approximate count, primary action switches based on streaming state, keyboard shortcuts (Esc stop, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter regenerate), prompt library as inline drawer with keyboard nav. Ava: update Figma. Marcus: prototype. Jorge: add abort API docs. Sam: produce a11y checklist. Ava (Design): Thanks! Updated figma link (with focus states and token pill): https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/playground-chat-ui-v2 — added notes on copy and keyboard shortcuts. :thumbsup: Marcus (Frontend): Thanks — will post prototypes in this thread when ready. Rina (PM): If any blockers call out here. Otherwise we'll roll this into next sprint planning.
